newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Trucks sees increased competition.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Trucks sees increased competition.

text.p: Volvo Trucks, a unit of Swedish automotive group AB Volvo, said on Thursday it expected increased competition on the European truck market next year, but saw total European sales flat in 1997 compared with 1996.
"The competition situation ahead of next year is changed. All manufacturers have new models out on the market," Volvo Trucks' spokesman Stefan Lorentzson told Reuters.
In addition, U.S. manufacturer Paccar has entered Europe by stepping into Dutch DAF.
"We know Paccar from the U.S., but we do not know what steps it is planning to take in Europe. All in all, this makes the market tougher and pricing could be affected," Lorentzson said.
But Volvo Trucks expected that the total European market next year will remain in line with this year's trends, possibly with a small decrease, he said.
"In 1997, the European market will probably be in line with 1996 trends, that is around 170,000 heavy trucks. There could be a slight slip, but nothing dramatic," Lorentzson said.
